landing.meta.title: CVsprings — Deterministic CV screening
landing.meta.description: Rules-based CV screening for boutique recruitment agencies. Same input, same output, every time. Built for EU AI Act and GDPR compliance.
landing.metastrip.engine: ENGINE: RULES-BASED · NO LLM IN CANDIDATE PATH
landing.hero.title: Screening that gives the same answer twice.
landing.hero.lede: CVsprings scores candidates with a transparent, rules-based engine — no language model ever reads your candidates' data. Same CV, same job profile, same result. Every time. Provable.
landing.hero.note: Built for boutique agencies in the Benelux & DACH · EU AI Act ready
landing.repro.label: Reproducibility check demonstration
landing.repro.title: Reproducibility check
landing.clauses.title: Compliance isn't a feature we added. It's the architecture.
landing.clauses.c1.label: CL. 01 — TRANSPARENCY
landing.clauses.c1.title: Every score is explainable
landing.clauses.c1.body: Each candidate assessment shows exactly which rules fired, which skills matched, and why. No black box, no "the model decided." Your client asks why — you answer in one click.
landing.clauses.c2.label: CL. 02 — REPRODUCIBILITY
landing.clauses.c2.title: Same input, same output
landing.clauses.c2.body: The extraction and scoring engine is fully deterministic. Re-run any assessment months later for an audit and get byte-identical results. Try that with an LLM-based screener.
landing.clauses.c3.label: CL. 03 — AUDITABILITY
landing.clauses.c3.title: A trail regulators can read
landing.clauses.c3.body: Every action is logged against a formal assessment schema aligned with EU AI Act traceability requirements. Export the full audit trail per candidate or per role.
landing.clauses.c4.label: CL. 04 — DATA MINIMISATION
landing.clauses.c4.title: Candidate data stays in the EU
landing.clauses.c4.body: No candidate data is sent to third-party AI providers — because there are none in the pipeline. Processing is GDPR-scoped by design, with per-candidate deletion on request.

landing.recording.lede: One pass through the engine: a role defined explicitly, a candidate scored with every point traced to the line that earned it, the audit log, and the bias report. Nothing is edited between steps.

landing.statement.title: Why we don't use AI to read CVs.
landing.statement.p1: Most screening tools put a language model between your candidates and your shortlist. It reads the CV, forms an impression, and returns a score it cannot explain and will not repeat. Run the same CV twice and you can get two different answers.
landing.statement.p2_html: Under the EU AI Act, screening candidates is high-risk — when it's done by an AI system. The obligations that follow are not light: risk management, data governance, technical documentation, logging, human oversight, conformity assessment. And a good part of that lands on you, the agency deploying the tool, not only on the vendor who built it.
landing.statement.p3_html: So we made the unfashionable choice: a rules engine you configure. The thresholds, the weights, the knockouts are yours, written down in advance, applied the same way to every candidate. No model reads the CV. Nothing infers, because there is nothing to infer from — the rules are the rules, and they run exactly as written.
landing.statement.p4: Which is the point. Every score comes with the rule that produced it. The audit trail is attested by the server, not supplied by the browser. And a determinism check runs before every release: same CV, same rules, same score, or the build doesn't ship.

bias.meta.title: CVsprings · Bias & Monitoring
bias.hero.title: Bias & monitoring
bias.hero.lede: This page explains exactly how CVsprings produces its scores, the design choices that reduce bias risk, the limitations we know about, and a live view of scoring consistency computed from your own organization’s audit data.
bias.method.title: 1 · How scores are produced
bias.method.intro_html: CVsprings uses a deterministic, rule-based matching engine — not a machine-learning model. The same input always produces the same score, and the same rules are applied identically to every CV. The pipeline:
bias.method.extraction_html: Text extraction. Plain text is extracted from the uploaded PDF or DOCX. Images — including photos — are never extracted or processed; scanned image-only CVs are rejected with an error rather than scored.
bias.method.subscores_html: Four sub-scores, each computed by transparent rules:
bias.method.keywords_html: Keywords — the 40 most frequent meaningful words and word pairs are extracted from your job description (common stop-words removed) and looked up in the CV text; the score is the percentage found.
bias.method.skills_html: Skills — a curated list of 168 named skills is checked against the job description; those the JD mentions are then looked up in the CV; the score is the percentage matched (a neutral 50 is used when the JD names none of the listed skills).
bias.method.experience_html: Experience — patterns such as “7 years of experience” and seniority words (director, principal, lead, senior, junior…) are detected in both texts and compared, producing a heuristic 0–100 value.
bias.method.education_html: Education — the highest qualification keyword found (PhD > Master > Bachelor > diploma/certificate) is compared between CV and JD requirements.
bias.method.overall_html: The overall score is the weighted average of the four sub-scores using the weights you set (default 40/30/20/10); the verdict bands (“Excellent/Good/Partial/Poor Match”) are fixed thresholds on that number. Each saved record stores the weights and the scoring-engine version used, so any score can be reconstructed later.
bias.anon.title: What Anonymize removes
bias.anon.intro_html: When the Anonymize toggle is on, the following are stripped from the CV text before scoring:
bias.anon.list_html: Removed: email addresses · phone numbers · URLs (incl. social profiles) · address-like lines (street number + street word) · standalone year numbers 1940–2015 (birth-year range) · standalone name lines (2–4 capitalized words on their own line). Photos are never processed regardless of this setting, because only text is extracted.
bias.anon.gaps_html: Anonymize is a text-level filter with known gaps — see the limitations section below for what it cannot remove.
bias.mitigations.title: 2 · Design mitigations
bias.mitigations.demographics_html: No demographic inputs. CVsprings does not ask for, collect, or use any demographic data (gender, ethnicity, age, disability status) anywhere in the product.
bias.mitigations.identical_html: Identical treatment within a batch. Every CV in a batch is scored with the same extraction rules, the same job description, and the same weights — there is no per-candidate variation in how the engine behaves.
bias.mitigations.anonymize_html: Anonymization option to strip contact details and name lines before scoring (see above for exactly what is removed).
bias.mitigations.human_html: Human decision requirement. No score is ever converted into a decision automatically. Decisions (shortlist / hold / reject) exist only as explicit recruiter input, and each saved record attributes its review to the signed-in user.
bias.mitigations.immutable_html: Immutable records. Scores, weights and provenance fields cannot be edited after a record is saved; only the recruiter’s decision and note can change, and changes are kept in an append-only history.
bias.limits.title: 3 · Known limitations
bias.limits.intro: We list these candidly because deployers need them to use the tool responsibly:
bias.limits.vocabulary_html: Vocabulary sensitivity. The engine matches words, not meaning. A candidate who describes the right experience in different words than the job description scores lower than one who mirrors the JD’s vocabulary. Non-native phrasing or unconventional CV styles can be penalized for the same reason.
bias.limits.jdWording_html: Scores vary with JD wording. Because keywords are extracted from the job description by frequency, rephrasing the JD changes the keyword set and therefore the scores. Compare candidates only within the same JD and weights.
bias.limits.proxies_html: Anonymization cannot remove all proxies. University names, employer names, club memberships, languages, employment gaps, names mentioned mid-sentence, and other indirect signals remain in the text and can correlate with protected characteristics.
bias.limits.overStrip_html: Anonymize can remove legitimate data. The birth-year filter (1940–2015) also removes ordinary dates in that range — e.g. an older graduation year — which can slightly change the experience signal for the same CV.
bias.limits.heuristic_html: Heuristic experience/education detection. Years of experience and qualifications are detected by text patterns; unusual formats can be missed. Verify tenure and qualifications in interviews rather than relying on the sub-scores.
bias.limits.outcomes_html: No outcome-level bias detection. CVsprings does not collect demographic data, so it cannot measure whether outcomes differ across demographic groups. We recommend that clients periodically review their decision outcomes against their own equality-monitoring data and processes.
bias.limits.warning: A high or low score is a signal about text similarity to the job description — it is not a verdict on the person. Always review the underlying CV before acting on a score.
bias.monitor.title: 4 · Scoring consistency in your organization
bias.monitor.signin_html: Sign in via the <a0>main app</a0> to view monitoring data computed from your organization’s own audit records.
bias.monitor.note_html: What this shows: scoring consistency within your own audit data — how scores are distributed per role and how your team’s shortlist decisions relate to score bands. It is not a demographic bias audit — CVsprings does not collect demographic data.
bias.disclaimer_html: This page documents actual product behaviour and is not legal advice. See the <a0>EU AI Act compliance page</a0> for how these features map to provider obligations.

integrations.meta.title: CVsprings · Integrations & API
integrations.hero.title: Integrations & API
integrations.hero.lede: How CVsprings connects to recruiting workflows — what works today, and where we’re headed. Each capability is tagged so you always know what’s live versus planned. We have no ATS partnerships yet; platform names below indicate intended targets only.
integrations.today.title: Today
integrations.today.intro_html: Integration today means manual upload and export:
integrations.today.upload: Single & batch CV upload (PDF/DOCX) scored against a job description.
integrations.today.csv: CSV export of ranked results and the full audit log.
integrations.today.reports: Professional branded PDF candidate assessment reports.
integrations.today.note: There is no programmatic API or automated ATS push/pull yet — everything below is direction, not a live capability.
integrations.api.title: Public REST API
integrations.api.body: Authenticate with a per-org API key and call documented endpoints to submit CVs/JDs and retrieve scores, audit records, and templates — the same analysis the web app produces, programmatically.
integrations.api.use: Use case: embed CVsprings scoring into your own recruiting tooling. A draft technical specification (auth, endpoints, schemas, webhooks, limits) is available to prospects — request it via the contact below.
integrations.webhooks.title: Webhooks
integrations.webhooks.body: Register a callback URL and receive a signed notification when an analysis (especially a large batch) finishes, instead of polling.
integrations.webhooks.use: Use case: trigger the next step in your workflow the moment results are ready.
integrations.ats.title: Native ATS connectors
integrations.ats.body: The generic pattern: your ATS pushes a new application plus the job description to CVsprings → CVsprings scores it → the score and the recruiter’s decision are written back to the ATS record, so scoring appears inside the tool your team already uses.
integrations.ats.platforms_html: Platforms we intend to support (examples of common ATS targets — not existing integrations or partnerships): Greenhouse, Lever, Teamtailor, Recruitee, Personio, SmartRecruiters.
integrations.ats.use: Priority follows client demand — tell us which ATS you use.
integrations.middleware.title: Middleware (Zapier / Make)
integrations.middleware.body: Once the public API exists, a Zapier/Make connector could bridge CVsprings to many tools without a bespoke integration per platform.
integrations.middleware.use: Use case: a lower-effort path to broad coverage while native connectors mature.
integrations.sequencing.title: Sequencing
integrations.sequencing.intro_html: We commit to phases, not dates. Order reflects dependency; priority within exploration follows what clients ask for.
integrations.sequencing.p3note: Built for the platform the most clients request.
integrations.request.title: Request an integration / API access
integrations.request.body: Integrations are prioritised by demand. Tell us which ATS you use and what you’d like to automate — it directly informs what we build first.
integrations.request.note_html: API usage, once available, is subject to the same human-oversight principle as the rest of the product: scores are advisory and all hiring decisions remain with the recruiter. See the <a0>compliance page</a0>.
integrations.request.ctaFallback: Contact us via the in-app About panel
